description: Determine the Cartesian equation of the locus of a point M with affix z=x+iy satisfying a given relation involving z and its conjugate, and identify the locus in the complex plane.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math textbook, Chapter 1 (complex numbers, algebraic form) — exercises only
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-25

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find the equation of the locus of the point } M \text{ with affix } z \text{ satisfying } (2-i)z+(2+i)\bar z = 6. \text{ Identify the locus of } M.
exercises.technique: Substitute z=x+iy and \bar z=x-iy, expand, and simplify to a linear (or other) Cartesian equation in x and y; then identify the curve/line it describes.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find the equation of the locus of the point } M \text{ with affix } z \text{ satisfying } (1+3i)z+(1-3i)\bar z = 4. \text{ Identify the locus of } M.
exercises.technique: Substitute z=x+iy and \bar z=x-iy, expand, and simplify to a linear Cartesian equation in x and y; then identify the curve/line it describes.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find the equation of the locus of the point } M \text{ with affix } z \text{ satisfying } (z-1+2i)(\bar z-1-2i) = 2. \text{ Identify the locus of } M.
exercises.technique: Substitute z=x+iy, expand the product (this is of the form |z-z_0|^2=r^2), and simplify to the equation of a circle.

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find the equation of the locus of the point } M \text{ with affix } z \text{ satisfying } z^2+(\bar z)^2 = 2. \text{ Identify the locus of } M.
exercises.technique: Substitute z=x+iy, expand z^2 and (\bar z)^2 using i^2=-1, and simplify to a Cartesian equation in x and y (a hyperbola).

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find the equation of the locus of the point } M \text{ with affix } z \text{ satisfying } (1+iz)(1-i\bar z) = 2. \text{ Identify the locus of } M.
exercises.technique: Substitute z=x+iy, expand the product using i^2=-1, and simplify to a Cartesian equation in x and y (a circle).

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find the equation of the locus of the point } M \text{ with affix } z \text{ satisfying } (z-1)^2+(\bar z-1)^2 = 4. \text{ Identify the locus of } M.
exercises.technique: Substitute z=x+iy, expand both squares using i^2=-1, and simplify to a Cartesian equation in x and y (a hyperbola).
